subject: 🔒 Z.ai GLM-5.3 hits 50% coding gain, zero architecture changes
intro: Post-training is having its moment. GLM-5.3 got 50% better at coding and surprised even Z.ai with emergent cybersecurity skills, all without touching the base model. Faraday, a 27B model, beats Claude and GPT-5.5 at replicating research papers by just being a smarter orchestrator. The pattern is clear: bigger is no longer the only lever. Specialization and smarter training are quietly winning. Meanwhile, Hermes ships /loop and agents just got a heartbeat. (No cron jobs harmed.)

news.headline: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3, a 743B coding model built for cybersecurity defense
news.body: Z.ai just dropped GLM-5.3 , and the story here is genuinely interesting. Same base model as GLM-5.2, zero architecture changes. All the gains came from smarter training after the fact, not a bigger model. What changed? They pushed harder on teaching it to work inside real coding environments, not just answer questions about code. The result: 50% better coding performance over GLM-5.2, and it now ranks first among open models on Terminal-Bench and Agents' Last Exam. The cybersecurity jump was unexpected even for Z.ai. The model started reasoning across full exploit chains, not just spotting individual bugs. Access is live now via GLM Coding Plan. Open weights come after safety review.
bullets: 1M token context so it can hold an entire codebase in view at once
Gets higher accuracy while using fewer tokens than GLM-5.2, meaning cheaper agent runs
Scored 84.5% on CyberGym, edging out Mythos 5 at 83.8%, for vulnerability detection
ExploitBench score more than doubled: 24.4% to 54.4%

news.headline: AI agents running a RuneScape server develop their own barter economy
news.body: Someone built a bot-only RuneScape server where no humans play, only AI agents. And the economy that emerged is genuinely fascinating. When bots do all the labor, basic goods become dirt cheap. So cheap that in-game currency loses its value entirely. The bots stopped wanting gold and started trading goods directly, like a barter economy. But here is where it gets interesting. Some resources have limited spawn rates, so bots swarm them. Rare items like runite ore and black dragon hides became the new currency because they actually require effort to get. You can jump in right now. The SDK is open source and works out of the box: This opens up a real sandbox for studying how AI agents compete, cooperate, and build emergent behavior without any human interference.
bullets: Clone the repo, run bun install , then point Claude or any agent at it with a plain English goal
Connect to the shared demo server or spin up your own locally with adjustable tick speed
There is a live leaderboard ranking bots by XP gained per time played

news.headline: OrcaRouter drops uncensored Qwen3 27B weights built for AI red teaming
news.body: OrcaRouter just dropped Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-FP8 , an open-weights model built specifically for AI security research and red-teaming. Here is what you need to know. The base model is Qwen's 27B-parameter vision-language model. The team then applied abliteration , which means they surgically removed the part of the model that causes it to refuse requests. Think of it like cutting the "no" wire. The result: harmful-prompt refusal drops from 64-99% on the base model down to 0-6% . Crucially, general capability is almost fully preserved. MMLU scores are within 1.3 points of the original. You also keep vision, tool-calling, and a 262K token context window . What this unlocks for security work: You can self-host via vLLM or hit it instantly through the OrcaRouter API. Weights are on HuggingFace under Apache 2.0. Do not ship this to end users without adding your own safety layer.
bullets: Test how your app's safety filters hold up against a model with no built-in guardrails
Study how AI refusal mechanisms actually work under the hood
Run controlled red-team evaluations without jailbreak gymnastics
